Definition: second person singular present of G1510; thou art:--art, be.
BiblicalUsage: This is the word thou art, the second person of the verb to be, and the Greek text never spells it as a separate lemma: it always appears as a form of the verb to be. The tempter says, If thou be the Son of God, and John's messengers ask Jesus, Art thou he that should come. The word is small, but it carries the question of who Jesus is.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the question art thou is still the question, because everything turns on who Jesus is, and I answer that He is the Son of God.
